attribution.note: Marcus wrote this in his own post, referring to himself in the third person. It is his own endorsed claim about his track record.

semantics.note: The claim keeps his wording, including the 'from day 1' scope. It is a retrospective observation about what he has said, not a claim that LLMs are in fact oversold.

contract.note: Reading 'day 1' as the outset of his public LLM commentary is an ordinary, fair reading. It correctly bars his own retrospective assertion from proving itself. The result turns on identifying that outset, which the speaker did not supply.

evidence.note: Quanta (2020) documents Marcus mocking GPT-2's common-sense failures in October 2019 and calls him a critic of AI hype. This shows early skepticism but not that it began at the outset of his LLM commentary.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows independent reporting of Marcus deriding GPT-2 in October 2019, months after GPT-2's debut. It does not establish when his LLM commentary began, or that he called LLMs oversold from that start. No contradicting earlier record is presented. The from-the-outset claim is therefore neither established nor refuted.

attribution.note: Marcus wrote this himself in his own post, as part of a rhetorical list.

semantics.note: This is a factual element pulled out of a rhetorical question. The proposition keeps his wording, including 'unexplained', with no added date.

contract.note: Tying the claim to the February 20–21 incident and reading 'unexplained' as its status when he published is an ordinary reading. Another possible reading is 'unexplained at onset'. The contract handles a malfunction that had been explained as mixed, which is fair.

evidence.note: ITPro, February 21, 2024: ChatGPT gave nonsensical, gibberish answers. This supports the meltdown part. Its 'nobody knows why' framing came before OpenAI's explanation.

OpenAI status update dated February 21, 2024 attributes the malfunction to an optimization bug that caused incorrect inference-kernel results. A public causal explanation therefore came before Marcus's February 22 post.

reviews.rationale: The meltdown part holds: contemporaneous reporting documents ChatGPT giving incoherent responses on February 20–21, 2024. The 'unexplained' part does not hold: OpenAI's incident record gave a causal explanation (an optimization bug in token selection) on February 21, before the February 22 post. Under the contract this compound claim is mixed.
